Here are my suggestions and they're all just what I would do. Nothing in here written in blood or stone says you have to do them but they'd all be smart things to do:

  1. Your new Bike, Turn it into a minimalist prepper system. A Bug Out Bike, if you will. Have a few supplies in saddlebags that you'd need if you had to literally just bonk out. Have some extra tubes, a couple of tools to work on your bike on the fly, a little gear for shelter building...stuff like that.

  2. Set aside $1k for a small emergency cash stash. You'll already be doing better than most in that area. Hide it in small increments around your place, you and your bike. Learn how to be sneaky about where you stash it and how much.

  3. Get a bug-out/INCH bag together. This should be all the rest of your stuff that you'll need in an emergency. If something happens and you decide that your situation isn't safe and you have to run, this is the bag you'll grab, hop on your bike and pedal like your hair is on fire and your ass is catching. A Bug-Out Bag will be more food and water intensive while the INCH (I'm Never Coming Home) bag will be more tool-heavy. In the INCH situation, you'll be getting food on the run by means of hunting, fishing or foraging. Your water situation will have to rely on water filtration and purification by fire or chemical means.

  4. Get your Every Day Carry (EDC) kit together if you haven't already. Look at what you currently have in terms of maybe what's in your wallet, your pocketknife if you have one, a good small flashlight, bandanna, watch (Anything by Casio in the G-shock series or Victorinox works and works well), small defensive tool (like a kubotan), keys, etc. Look at what you'll actually use every day and what you'll use situationally like when you need to dress up. You should probably create both. Experiment. See what it is you're comfortable with and go from there.

  5. Build a good Food and Water storage system for your home. In an emergency or disaster, you'll need at least a month or two's worth of food and water. You have five grand you can play with and, believe me, if you do a search for things like warehouse surplus places that just give away food they'll discard at the end of the day, you can still save some of that scratch for more gear that you may need around your place.

  6. Invest in Escape and Evasion tools and knowledge. Learn how to survive anywhere. The books are cheap enough and will impart some pretty bombproof skills

  7. Speaking of Skills, learn and master at least one. I would say anything medical or something in the realm of sewing. People will need clothing and shoes as well as medical care. Learn those and you can almost name your price if things go south and they're needed.

This list isn't exhaustive but it something I think might just benefit you. If you have anything left over after getting this stuff together, stash it with your cash and never use it unless it's a bona fide emergency situation like a disaster or something like that.

Hope that helps. If you have any questions, hit me up.
